newsitem.title: ALBANIA: US wants Albania parties to take part in elections.
newsitem.headline: US wants Albania parties to take part in elections.

text.p: The United States urged all Albanian political parties to take part in early general elections on June 29 seen as vital to save the Balkan nation from a return to chaos, and honour the election results.
The U.S. Embassy in Tirana said the international community expected Albanians behaved responsibly for their own future.
"We expect all political parties to participate fully in the elections and honour their results," the embassy said in a statement.
"The basic responsibilities lie with the Albanian parties themselves," it added.
Bickering Albanian parties want their conditions to be met before they enter the elections.

A nine-party government of national unity led by Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino is striving to create conditions for the vote amid pressure from some parties to lift a state of emergency and end voting before 6 p.m.

A state of emergency was imposed in March to stop rioting and looting that spread across Europe's poorest nation, sparked by people losing their savings in the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes.

"There can be no free elections with the state of emergency and we want free elections that will assure the victory of the Socialist Party," Pandeli Majko, the party's public affairs secretary told a rally of up to 20,000 in Tirana on Tuesday.
But Parliament Speaker Pjeter Arbnori said on Wednesday he did not intend to summon the dissolved parliament to lift the state of emergency.
"We cannot lift the state of emergency before restoring the constitutional order," Arbnori told Albanian television. "The state of emergency is a barrier to none, only to violence."
Despite their protest, most of the Socialist speakers, including chairman Fatos Nano, pledged to lead the party to victory on June 29 and give back voters a normal Albania.
The Socialist-led opposition boycotted elections a year ago last May, saying the ruling Democrats of President Sali Berisha rigged the vote.
The American embassy made it clear Washington would not tolerate another boycott.

"All talk of boycott should be left behind. The word boycott should be stricken from the Albanian vocabulary," the statement quoted U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Europe and Canada, John Kornblum as saying.
